summary: Reproduces a memorandum issued on 2 July 1987 by the Assistant Secretary of Defense for Command, Control, Communications, and Intelligence to the Director of the Defense Communications Agency, on the DoD position on Open Systems Interconnection protocols. It is distributed for information only and replaces RFC 945.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 1039 reproduces a Defense Department memorandum about OSI protocols. The memo sets an experimental policy for using them alongside existing DoD protocols and describes a possible transition.

subtitle: Reproduces a DoD memo adopting OSI protocols as experimental co-standards.

tldr.problem: Progress in OSI specifications and implementations led the Department of Defense to revise its policy for host-to-host data communication protocols.
tldr.mechanism: The memo adopts OSI message handling and file transfer protocols as experimental co-standards to matching DoD protocols and requests transition work.
tldr.outcome: It states an intention for OSI to become a full co-standard after GOSIP approval and later the sole mandatory suite, while preserving interoperation with DoD protocols.

sections.title: The Memorandum and Its Context
sections.content:
RFC 1039 reproduces a memorandum issued on 2-JUL-87 from the Assistant Secretary of Defense for Command, Control, Communications, and Intelligence to the Director of the Defense Communications Agency. It is distributed for information only.

The memo notes rapid progress in protocols based on the ISO Open Systems Interconnection (OSI) model. It says the Government OSI Profile dated 22 April 1987 contained enough information to specify and acquire interoperable OSI message-handling and file-transfer implementations.
sections.plainLanguage: The RFC is a copy of a DoD memorandum from July 1987. It discusses how new OSI protocols relate to existing DoD protocol standards.

sections.title: Experimental Co-Standards
sections.content:
The memo modifies an earlier policy by adopting OSI message-handling and file-transfer protocols, with their underlying GOSIP protocols, as experimental co-standards to DoD protocols that provide similar services. It names MIL-STDs 1777, 1778, 1780 and 1781.

The OSI protocols could be specified in addition to, instead of, or as an optional alternative to DoD protocols where current applicability statements allowed. The memo cites limited operational experience and a limited operational, testing and security environment as reasons for experimental status.
sections.plainLanguage: OSI protocols could be used alongside or instead of similar DoD protocols on an experimental basis. The memo says experience and testing were still limited.

sections.title: Transition Plan and Follow-up
sections.content:
The memo intends to make OSI a full co-standard once GOSIP is formally approved as a Federal Information Processing Standard. Two years after that, it expects OSI to become the sole mandatory interoperable suite, while preserving interoperability with DoD protocols for the expected life of systems that support them.

It requests a DoD-OSI transition plan, coordination with OSI groups, security work and sharing of early implementation experience. It says final implementation details will come later in a DoD Directive.
sections.plainLanguage: The memo describes a phased transition, first allowing both protocol families and later making OSI the required suite. It also calls for interoperation with existing DoD systems.

references.text: Latham, D., "A DoD Statement on Open Systems Interconnection Protocols", RFC 945, obsoleted by RFC 1039.
